biomni2025science.notes: DISCREPANCY: the Science version is dated 2026, not 2025 (Science 393(6813), eadz4351, published 20 Aug 2026), and its title differs from the preprint. Preprint title: 'Biomni: a general-purpose biomedical AI agent' (bioRxiv https://doi.org/10.1101/2025.05.30.656746, posted 2 Jun 2025). 28 authors, first Kexin Huang, last Jure Leskovec. Science uses an e-locator (eadz4351), not a page range. The JSON key keeps the requested '2025' label, but the year in the reference must be 2026. The science.org page itself was not fetched; PubMed and Crossref agree on every field.

bixbench2025.reference: Mitchener, L. et al. BixBench: a comprehensive benchmark for LLM-based agents in computational biology. Preprint at https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2503.00096 (2025).
bixbench2025.notes: arXiv ID 2503.00096 confirmed. v1 posted 28 Feb 2025; latest is v3 (8 Oct 2025). v3 lists 9 authors: Mitchener, Laurent, Andonian, Tenmann, Narayanan, Wellawatte, White, Sani, Rodriques. Some older listings show 8 authors without Andonian; with 'et al.' this does not change the citation. Original capitalization is 'BixBench: a Comprehensive Benchmark for LLM-based Agents in Computational Biology'. The sentence-case form above is exactly how Nature Methods cited it (Saez-Rodriguez et al. 2026, ref. list). No peer-reviewed version found: arXiv has no journal_ref or DOI, Crossref bibliographic search found nothing, and OpenReview lists it only as 'CoRR 2025'. Semantic Scholar was rate-limited and DBLP was bot-gated, so those two indexes were not checked. Do not confuse with 'BixBench3' (arXiv:2608.25286), a separate later work.

cemri2025.reference: Cemri, M. et al. Why do multi-agent LLM systems fail? In *Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 38* (NeurIPS, 2025).
cemri2025.notes: arXiv 2503.13657 confirmed (v1 17 Mar 2025, v3 26 Oct 2025; 13 authors, first Mert Cemri, last Ion Stoica). A peer-reviewed version exists: the NeurIPS 2025 virtual site lists it as a 'Spotlight Poster' with OpenReview id fAjbYBmonr. Secondary sources (mlanthology, search-engine summaries) place it in the Datasets & Benchmarks track, with proceedings published 23 Apr 2026; the official page shown did not state the track. Proceedings volume 38 follows Nature's own house style for NeurIPS 2025 papers (e.g. Nat. Biotechnol. s41587-026-03307-w cites 'Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 38 (NeurIPS, 2025)'). Page numbers NOT verified: the proceedings.neurips.cc entry could not be reached. If the arXiv form is preferred: 'Cemri, M. et al. Why do multi-agent LLM systems fail? Preprint at https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2503.13657 (2025).' Nature allows only one publication per reference number, so cite one form, preferably the NeurIPS version.

compbiobench.reference: Nair, S. et al. Agentic systems are adept at solving well-scoped, verifiable problems in computational biology. Preprint at bioRxiv https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.04.06.716850 (2026).
compbiobench.notes: Identified with high confidence. The bioRxiv abstract says 'We introduce CompBioBench, a benchmark of 100 diverse tasks for evaluating agentic systems in computational biology' (Genentech; corresponding author Gokcen Eraslan). v1 posted 9 Apr 2026, v2 posted 3 May 2026; no journal version yet (bioRxiv 'published' = NA). The DOI really uses bioRxiv's newer 10.64898 prefix (confirmed in Crossref), not 10.1101. 11 authors: Nair, Gunsalus, Orcutt-Jahns, Rossen, Lal, De Donno, Celik, Fletez-Brant, Xie, Corrada Bravo, Eraslan. The HF dataset file compbiobench.v1.tsv has exactly 100 question_id rows, including 'contaminated-rna-q1', 'encode-atac-pipeline-q1' and 'genome-coords-q1'. Leaderboard: https://huggingface.co/spaces/Genentech/compbiobench-leaderboard-v1. The task data can also be cited as a DOI'd dataset: 'Nair, S. et al. CompBioBench v1: a benchmark of 100 diverse, verifiable questions for agents for computational biology. Zenodo https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19443186 (2026).' Under the Nature Methods rule, cite leaderboard/HF URLs parenthetically in the text, not in the reference list.
